rows.name: xtlsdvc/default
rows.design: 500 units, 8 periods; analytic SE is the LSDV one
rows.mechanism: Two things. (1) Bias: the Stata plug-in for the deterministic part of the lagged outcome uses within-demeaned residuals, which keep each unit's mean error; the first-order correction then converges to -0.2195 where the exact LSDV inconsistency is -0.2353 (rho 0.5, seven usable periods), a bias that does not shrink with N. sp.xtlsdvc matches Stata xtlsdvc here; plug_in='consistent' removes it (tests/test_lsdvc_plug_in.py). (2) SE: the analytic SE is the LSDV one and ignores the estimated correction, as in Stata; the function warns and offers bootstrap=.

rows.name: xtlsdvc/consistent
rows.design: 500 units, 8 periods; analytic SE is the LSDV one
rows.mechanism: SE only. plug_in='consistent' removes the bias (bias/SD -0.07) but the analytic SE is still the LSDV one, which ignores the estimated correction (documented, warned). Row xtlsdvc/consistent-bootstrap is the calibrated combination.

rows.name: xtlsdvc/bootstrap
rows.design: 500 units, 8 periods; parametric bootstrap SE; B = 200
rows.mechanism: Bias only. The parametric bootstrap SE is calibrated (SE/SD 0.93) but the default Stata plug-in leaves a bias of 0.58 SD at 500 units; see xtlsdvc/default.

rows.name: panel/fe-driscoll-kraay
rows.design: 50 units, 60 periods, serially correlated period shocks in x1 and the error
rows.mechanism: Known small-T property of the Driscoll-Kraay HAC. The variance is a Bartlett HAC of the 60 period sums of the scores at the default lag 3 (a hand computation on one draw gives 0.0444 against the reported 0.0448). With serially correlated period shocks in the regressor and the error (rho 0.5 each) the kernel truncates and down-weights the autocovariances and the HAC is biased down at T = 60.

rows.name: mmqreg/q25
rows.design: location-scale; the 0.25 quantile slope is 0.5 + 0.3 z(0.25)
rows.mechanism: Incidental-parameter bias of order 1/T, not the SE (SE/SD 0.95). The scale equation is fitted on absolute within residuals with unit effects estimated from 8 observations each. Mean error at the 0.25 quantile: 0.069 with 4 periods, 0.035 with 8, 0.010 with 20, none with 40 (1,600 observations throughout). The median row is unaffected. Now stated in the mmqreg notes.
